corePages.headline: Am Flughafen
corePages.bodyGerman:
Guten Tag! Ich heiße Thomas Müller. Wie heißen Sie?

Guten Tag! Ich heiße Alex und ich komme aus Indien.

Freut mich, Sie kennenzulernen!
corePages.bodyEnglish:
Good day! My name is Thomas Müller. What's your name?

Good day! My name is Alex and I come from India.

Pleased to meet you!
corePages.culturalTip: Capitalized 'Sie' = formal you. 'du' is for friends, family and children.

corePages.headline: Die Kernwörter
corePages.bodyEnglish: The five words that carry every first conversation.

corePages.headline: Sie vs du
corePages.bodyEnglish: German has two 'you'. Formal 'Sie' (always capitalized!) takes verb + -en like they: 'Wie heißen Sie?' — 'wohnen Sie'. Informal 'du' takes -st / -t: 'Wie heißt du?' — 'wohnst du'. First meetings with adults = Sie, until invited to use du.
corePages.culturalTip: Getting the form wrong isn't rude, but staying on 'du' too early can be. When unsure: Sie.

corePages.headline: Sich verabschieden
corePages.bodyEnglish: 'Auf Wiedersehen' is the safe formal goodbye anywhere. 'Tschüss' is casual — friends and family only. In the south you'll also hear 'Servus' for both hello and goodbye.

patterns.title: Sich vorstellen
patterns.formula: Ich heiße + [Name] + und ich komme aus + [Land/Stadt].
patterns.explanationEnglish: The standard self-introduction. The 'und' joins two full clauses — each keeps its own verb position.

examples.german: Ich heiße Lukas und ich komme aus Wien.
examples.english: My name is Lukas and I come from Vienna.

examples.german: Ich heiße Anna und ich komme aus Berlin.
examples.english: My name is Anna and I come from Berlin.

patterns.title: Nachfragen (formal)
patterns.explanationEnglish: W-question word first, verb second — the V2 skeleton you'll meet in section 2.

practice.explanationEnglish: 'Ich heiße …' introduces your name. 'komme' needs 'aus', 'wohnen' needs a place.

practice.prompt: Which goodbye fits a job interview?
practice.explanationEnglish: Formal setting = 'Auf Wiedersehen'. 'Tschüss' and 'Servus' are casual.
Stranger + formal = 'Wie heißen Sie?' — note the capital S.
